metaData.originalTitle: 体验完腾讯发布的 Marvis 助手，我发现个人 AI 的尽头是操作系统
metaData.title: After Experiencing Tencent's Marvis Assistant, I Realize the Endgame of Personal AI is the Operating System
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tencent's Marvis assistant deeply integrates with the operating system's underlying layers through six out-of-the-box Agents, elevating personal AI from a Q&A interface to a device task scheduling layer, enabling system-level operations like file search, system configuration, and cross-device control via natural language.
metaData.summary: This article provides a detailed review of Tencent's newly launched Marvis AI assistant, positioned as an 'operating system-level personal AI assistant' and developed by the team behind the 14-year-old App Store, Yingyongbao. Marvis comes with six specialized Agents (PM, File, Computer, APP, Search, Browser) that work out of the box without requiring users to build workflows. Core capabilities include deep integration with system information and configuration entries, allowing direct modification of system settings; powerful local file search supporting multi-dimensional fuzzy searches by file name, document content, and text within images; cross-device control enabling a phone to take over a computer desktop in real-time; support for custom automated tasks and Skill extensions; and two security options: Efficiency Mode (cloud-based large model) and Privacy Mode (on-device model). The article argues that Marvis represents the evolution of personal AI from a 'Q&A interface' to a 'device task scheduling layer,' making computers truly begin to understand users.

mainPoints.point: Marvis is positioned as an operating system-level personal AI assistant, not just an ordinary chatbot.
mainPoints.explanation: The product deeply integrates with the system's underlying layers, enabling direct reading and modification of system configurations, hardware information, and the file system. This allows for system-level operations driven by natural language, such as disabling lock screen ads, checking battery health, and managing startup programs.

mainPoints.point: Six built-in Agents work collaboratively out of the box, lowering the barrier to entry.
mainPoints.explanation: Six Agents—PM, File, Computer, APP, Search, and Browser—each have distinct roles. Users don't need to build workflows or install plugins; they can complete complex task chains directly through natural language commands, making it highly user-friendly for ordinary users.

mainPoints.point: Local file search capabilities far exceed the system's built-in features, supporting multi-dimensional fuzzy retrieval.
mainPoints.explanation: It can search by file name, document content, and text or scenes within images. Even vague descriptions (e.g., 'the Black Myth: Wukong screenshot from the group chat two months ago') can be accurately located, addressing a major pain point of Windows' native search.

mainPoints.point: Cross-device control enables remote computer takeover via phone, offering a wealth of practical use cases.
mainPoints.explanation: The mobile app can view and control the computer desktop in real-time, even when the computer is locked. This is particularly useful for scenarios like remotely troubleshooting a family member's computer or installing software while away from home. If the computer loses its internet connection, the mobile app automatically switches to cloud mode.

mainPoints.point: Privacy Mode and Efficiency Mode can be switched as needed, balancing performance and data security.
mainPoints.explanation: In Privacy Mode, all retrieval, parsing, and recognition are handled by the local on-device model, ensuring data never leaves the device and works even offline. In Efficiency Mode, the cloud-based large model (Hunyuan + DeepSeek V4) handles planning while local execution ensures faster speeds.

keyQuotes: While others are busy competing over who has the better AI chatbot, Marvis aims to turn your entire computer into a partner you can command at will.
Personal AI shouldn't just be a Q&A interface; it should become the task scheduling layer within your device.
The focus of personal AI has never just been the AI; it's always been about the personal.
They can quickly train a smarter model, but they can't quickly build control over the PC's underlying layers and the mobile ecosystem.
Thirty years ago, Microsoft Bob tried to make computers easier for users to understand; thirty years later, Marvis is trying to make computers truly understand users.
